info.description:
Every function is called as `POST /api/v1/{category}/{service}/{func}` with a JSON body. The function name may instead be sent as `_func` in the body to `/api/v1/{category}/{service}`; when both are given, the body's `_func` is the one that runs.

The body is validated against the function's schema before it runs; a failure is a 400 whose `message` lists what is wrong.

**Tenancy.** On the client API, `fiduciary_id` is taken from the credential. A value sent in the body is overridden, so a key or token can never read or write another fiduciary's records. With a principal token, `user_id` is taken from the token too; a `user_id` in the body that does not match it is refused with 403. A function under `/api/v1/public/` has no credential and takes `fiduciary_id` from the body.

**GET.** A function may be called with GET only when it is a read; parameters then travel in the query string. Query values are strings and are validated like a body, so GET is documented only where every required parameter accepts a string, and only those parameters are listed. Everything else is POST-only (405 otherwise). A credential is never read from the query string.

**Errors.** Every error has the same body: `timestamp`, `status`, `error`, `message`, `path`.

**Authentication (client API).** Either an application API key (`X-API-Key` and `X-API-Secret` headers, together) or a data principal's bearer token. An API key carries scopes (READ, WRITE, PURGE); each function states the scope it needs, and a key without the scope gets 401. PURGE functions do not accept a principal token. Functions under `/api/v1/public/` need no credential.

**Authentication (admin API).** An operator bearer token from `login`. Every call must map to an ACTIVE operator; logout, deactivation or a password change revokes tokens at once. An account with MFA enabled must present an MFA-verified token for every function except `enrol_mfa`, `logout`, `verify_mfa`.

**Permissions (admin API).** Each function requires `<resource>:<action>`, checked against the operator's role in the roles table. `manage` implies `write`, and `write` implies `read`. The ADMIN role has full access. An operator bound to a fiduciary is confined to it; only a global ADMIN selects a fiduciary through the body.

**Bootstrap.** `/api/v1/bootstrap/` accepts initial setup only, with the bootstrap token (the `X-Bootstrap-Token` header, or `bootstrap_token` in the body).

`/api/v1/public/operator/sso_login` is the console's single sign-on; it is left out of the public document.

`x-unrouted` at the top of this document lists validator schemas that no service implements, and allowed functions that have no schema.

get.description:
LG-04: recompute the hash-chained ledger and report any break.

SEC-10: a tenant-scoped DPO or auditor may verify its own tenant's
rows (fiduciary_id is passed as a scope), while a global operator keeps
the platform-wide view. Neither learns other tenants' row ids. The walk
is newest-first so recent tampering cannot hide outside the limit.

Requires permission audit:read.

s.8(6) / Rule 7(1): intimate each affected Data Principal.

The principals are the ones the caller names (`user_ids`), or - when
none are named - every principal who ever granted the breach's
affected purpose. Each gets one BREACH_NOTIFICATION (or the breach's own
BREACH_NOTIFICATION_* category) carrying the breach's plain-language
steps, and a breach_affected_principals row; a principal already
notified for this breach is not notified twice.

Requires permission breach:write.

schema.title: Notify the principals affected by a personal data breach (s.8(6))

post.description:
s.8(6) / Rule 7(2): record that the Data Protection Board was intimated.

The 72-hour deadline column alone gave a clock with no way to stop it.
The intimation reference (the Board's acknowledgement or the filing id)
is mandatory; a late intimation is accepted and recorded as late.

P12-04: board_notified_at is the server's time of recording, never the
caller's. An intimation made earlier through another channel may be
asserted as intimated_at; it is kept in its own column and must fall
between detection and now.

P13-02: 'late' is decided by the recorded time only. An assertion is
unverified, so it is reported beside it as late_as_asserted - context
for the Board, never a way to turn a late record into an on-time one.

Requires permission breach:write.

schema.title: Record the Data Protection Board intimation of a breach (Rule 7)

post.description:
Status and resolution, plus the Rule 7 contents as they become known:
the Rule 7(1) intimation fields and the Rule 7(2)(b) detailed report.
`submit_detailed_report` stamps when that report went to the Board; it
needs every Rule 7(2)(b) field and can be stamped once.

Requires permission breach:write.

SA-09: the processor that executed a purge confirms it with evidence
(records affected, who confirmed, any error), so completion is recorded
as verified rather than assumed.

SEC-04: the confirmation is bound to the authenticated caller. An API
key must belong to the app assigned to the purge request, and the
confirming identity is taken from the credential, never from the free
`confirmed_by_entity_id` payload text.

Requires permission purge:write.

get.description:
Every ledger event about one consent record, grouped by purpose.

Ported from Consent-Manager (with its f0d65af grouping done here). An
event belongs to the trail when it is about the record's principal

their purpose_id ('ALL' when the row names none); each group lists the
purpose's name and the data categories it covers in the record's
policy. The principal id is used only to derive the pseudonym.

post.description:
CC-05: record a guardian verification, verifying it where the CMS can.

EXISTING_ACCOUNT is verified here: the guardian must already be a known
ADULT principal of this fiduciary. DIGILOCKER is verified by the
configured verifier (DIGILOCKER_VERIFY_URL), which must confirm the
reference and that the guardian is an adult. Anything else is stored as
an unverified assertion and cannot back a minor's consent.

Requires permission consent:write.

post.description:
GR-07: every category with its department and officer; unrouted
categories are reported with the DPO fallback.

Requires permission grievance:read.

GR-07: route a complaint category to a department and its officer.

`remove: true` deletes the rule, so the category falls back to the DPO.
The officer must be ACTIVE and belong to the fiduciary.

Requires permission operator:write.

GR-12: the principal rates how their resolved grievance was handled.

Requires permission grievance:write.

GR-04: attach supporting evidence to a grievance.

The file arrives base64-encoded in the JSON body, is checked against an
allow-list of types and the ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES limit, and is stored
under the export path by its SHA-256, never by the caller's file name.

Requires permission grievance:write.

LG-05/SA-14: crystallise a principal's hash-chained trail as evidence.

The certificate embeds the verified chain segment (an evidence trail),
environment metadata and an HMAC signature over that payload. The signing
key is a deployment secret (`certificate_signing_key`), not a client
secret the CMS serves; the algorithm and metadata are recorded so the
certificate is verifiable rather than a bare log dump. SEC-10: the chain
the certificate embeds is itself verified first — a certificate over a
tampered ledger is refused rather than signed without complaint.

Requires permission legal:write.

SEC-10: verify an evidence certificate's HMAC signature.

The signature is compared in constant time, and the certificate's
embedded evidence trail is re-derived against `audit_logs` — so a
certificate signed before the ledger was tampered with no longer returns
"valid" on signature alone. A chain break, or any embedded trail hash
that no longer exists in the ledger, is reported.

Requires permission legal:write.

CW-08: a processor's own endpoint, so a withdrawal reaches each
linked processor instead of one endpoint per category.

Requires permission notification:write.

SA-06: generate a TOTP secret for the caller and return the provisioning URI.

The secret is stored encrypted and shown exactly once; the account only
becomes mfa_enabled after a successful verify_mfa round-trip.
SA-05: revoke this session's token so it cannot be replayed until expiry.

SA-06: single sign-on through the organisation's OpenID Connect provider.

The console completes the provider's login and posts the id_token here.
It is verified against the provider's published keys (SSO_JWKS_URL), its
issuer (SSO_ISSUER) and this CMS as audience (SSO_AUDIENCE); its email
must belong to an ACTIVE operator. When the provider attests MFA (amr
claim) the session is MFA-verified; otherwise an account with TOTP
enrolled must still pass verify_mfa.

Requires permission operator:write.

SA-06: confirm a TOTP code and, once verified, issue a session token that
carries the mfa claim. The presenter must be the operator the secret belongs to.
